newsitem.title: HUNGARY: MOL roadshow may start April 21.
newsitem.headline: MOL roadshow may start April 21.

text.p: A source at the Hungarian privatisation agency APV said on Wednesday the date of April 21 mentioned in press reports as the start of a roadshow for the next MOL share offering was not inconsistent with plans.
"It would hurt the offering to say any date at this point," the source, who asked to remain anonymous, told Reuters. But he added the roadshow start date was "not far from APV's plans".

APV is expected to offer a further stake in MOL, the highest capitalised stock on the Budapest bourse, this year. Foreign oil firms will be prevented from gaining a majority stake to maintain MOL as the "national oil company".
The Hungarian business daily Napi Gazdasag reported on Wednesday that the company would launch an international roadshow for the issue from April 21. MOL officials declined to comment on the article.
A 12- to 18-percent stake is likely to be offered in the coming months. Altogether between 28 and 33 percent will be sold to financial investors and a yet-to-be-decided stake offered to MOL staff.
The newspaper said that the most likely date for the pricing of the offering would be May 6.

APV holds a 58 percent stake in MOL, which has an issued share capital of 98.4 billion forints. Hungary's privatisation law stipulates that the state must retain a minimum 25 percent stake in the company.
At 1021 GMT, MOL shares stood at 3,030 forints, up 10.
